text:
alex: Heads up — saw a suspicious authz result during a customer rewrap window. looks like an embeddings-scoped token was accepted on a /v1/chat route. sharing quick logs and a short repro.

riley: Ack. can you paste the request id + raw auth metadata?

alex: request_id=req_0a3f8c, infra logs: `auth.check -> token=tok_eb123, allowed_scopes=[embeddings.model:all], route=/v1/chat`, decision=ALLOW (policy matched fallback). KMS event window: rewrap key_id old=key-A new=key-B at 2026-02-14T01:12:10Z.

marta: Wait fallback policy matched? we have a deny-by-default per-route allowlist for chat routes. how did fallback get applied?

chris: Possible race between KMS tag update and authz cache invalidation. when we rewrap we re-tag allowed route metadata; if tag disappears momentarily the checker falls back to legacy merging logic.

alex: I think so. the authz decision path shows this path: `check_route_allowlist -> lookup_kms_tag(route) -> cache_miss -> fallback_merge_allowlist(token.tags)` which currently treats embeddings:* as compatible for some legacy routes (BUG).

sam: Can you paste the minimal repro curl?

alex: sure:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_eb123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}' -i
```

logs show `authz:fallback_merge=true` + `policy_evaluator:matched_legacy_set=[embeddings.*]`.

riley: omg. that rule was added ages ago to support multi-scope tokens during migration. We never tightened it to per-route model types.

marta: Impact? only customer X? time window?

alex: So far only one customer report (customer X), timeframe 2026-02-14 01:12:09-01:12:17Z (the rewrap window). approx 8s window. We saw ~12 allowed chat calls with embeddings-only tokens.

chris: Severity I'd call P1 for access-control correctness. Need hotfix: stop fallback_merge on any route with explicit allowlist, and invalidate authz cache on rewrap commit.

sam: +1. short-term mitigations: 1) emergency policy change to disable legacy-merge behavior globally 2) run backfill audit for tokens used during window 3) notify affected customer.

securitybot: [automated] Creating incident record INC-2026-0456 (severity=P1) and paging oncall.

riley: I can push a quick guard in the authenticator: if route has explicit allowlist, require explicit scope match; bypass old merge behavior. small code change in authz service. will open PR.

chris: Also add a check: if kms.rewrap flag is present in event stream and authz cache still has old tags, force immediate invalidation for keys involved.

alex: PR checklist candidate: unit test for embeddings-only token against chat route -> expect DENY; integration test that simulates KMS rewrap producing transient tag=absent; make sure no fallback allowed.

marta: Who will notify legal/compliance? this might be data exfil risk if chat responses include customer content.

sam: I'll notify compliance + support. draft notice to customer referencing INC-2026-0456, include timeline and ask if they observed any unexpected outputs.

riley: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/authz/pull/389 - contains guard + metric `authz.fallback_blocked` increment. deploying to canary now.

chris: Nice. also add alert when `authz.fallback_merge=true` increments > 1 in 1m. we want signal if this ever happens outside migration windows.

alex: Backfill query (SQL) I ran to find affected tokens: 
```
SELECT request_id, token_id, route, created_at
FROM auth_logs
WHERE created_at BETWEEN '2026-02-14 01:12:00' AND '2026-02-14 01:12:30'
  AND auth_decision='ALLOW'
  AND token_scopes LIKE '%embeddings.%'
  AND route LIKE '/v1/chat%';
```

marta: Good. save query in incident docs. we should also audit KMS rewrap pipeline: ensure tag writes are atomic and clients don't see untagged keys.

sam: Compliance asked for an immediate audit export. alex, can you dump auth logs for the window? any PII redaction?

alex: Dumping now to secure bucket s3://redwood-incident/INC-2026-0456/ with KMS encryption. removed payload bodies.

riley: Canary shows no new occurrences after guard deployed (10m observation). preparing rollback plan in case we need to revert.

chris: Postmortem action items: 1) remove legacy fallback entirely after migration cutoff 2) enforce per-model-type scoping in policy language (embeddings vs chat) 3) KMS rewrap: make write-tag idempotent and emit pre/post state events to stream 4) add e2e test for authz during rewrap windows 5) compliance notification template.

marta: assign owners: riley (hotfix + metric + unit tests), chris (KMS pipeline change), alex (audit/export + incident doc), sam (customer/compliance comms). I'll own the PM for follow-ups.

securitybot: [automated] Incident updated: severity=P1 -> actions assigned.

alex: Thanks. I also recommend a short-term warning metric for any token that has scopes set but no kms_tag present; that'll catch future partial-updates.

sam: Noted. I'll include in the customer message: apologizing, summary of root cause (KMS rewrap race + legacy merge rule), and next steps (audit, patch, mitigation).

riley: pushing to prod in ~12m after smoke test. will update when green. :thumbsup:

alex: Green, guard deployed to prod at 2026-02-14T01:34:22Z. No further incidents observed.

marta: Great work. postmortem pls include timeline + exact token ids (redacted) + follow-up dates.

chris: I'll schedule KMS pipeline changes in next sprint and add e2e tests.

sam: Customer notified. awaiting reply.

securitybot: [automated] Incident INC-2026-0456 status -> mitigated.

alex: Closing thread for now; will update when postmortem is ready.
